The '''1961–62 DDR-Oberliga''' was the 13th season of the [[DDR-Oberliga]], the first tier of [[East German football league system|league football]] in [[East Germany]]. It was the first season played in the traditional autumn-spring format again after the Oberliga had played for six seasons from 1955 to 1960 in the calendar year format instead, modelled on the system used in the [[Soviet Union]]. The league was played as a triple round with a home-and-away round and an additional round of games at neutral venues to allow for an earlier start.

The league was contested by fourteen teams. [[National People's Army]] club [[ASK Vorwärts Berlin]] won the championship, the club's second consecutive one and third overall, eventually winning six national East German championships overall.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrchamp.html |title= East Germany - List of Champions |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 20 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Meister" >{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/historie/ddr-fussball/meister/ |title= DDR-Meister |website=dfb.de |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |access-date= 20 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= East German champions}}</ref> On the strength of the 1961–62 title Vorwärts qualified for the [[1962–63 European Cup]] where the club was knocked out by [[Dukla Prague]] in the preliminary round. Eleventh-placed club [[Hallescher FC|SC Chemie Halle]] qualified for the [[1962–63 European Cup Winners' Cup]] as the seasons [[FDGB-Pokal]] winner and was knocked out by [[OFK Beograd]] in the preliminary round as well.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec196263.html |title= European Competitions 1962-63|website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 20 January 2016}}</ref>

[[Arthur Bialas]] of [[F.C. Hansa Rostock|SC Empor Rostock]] was the league's top scorer with 23 goals.<ref name="Goal" >{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/gdr-oberliga/ |title= DDDR » Oberliga » Torschützenkönige  |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 20 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga top scorers }}</ref>

The 1961–62 season saw the third-most games played in an Oberliga season, 273. Only 1950–51 and 1951–52 had there been more, 306 and 342, when the league consisted of 18 and 19 clubs. The season also saw the lowest-ever average attendance with 8,088 per match.<ref name="Fuwo" />

==Table==									
The 1961–62 season saw two newly promoted clubs, [[FC Rot-Weiss Erfurt|SC Turbine Erfurt]] and [[Lok Stendal|BSG Lokomotive Stendal]].<ref name="Ddr" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrhist.html |title= East Germany 1946-1990 |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 20 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielplan/gdr-oberliga-1961-1962-spieltag/26/ |title= DDR » Oberliga 1961–62 |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 20 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga 1961–62}}</ref>
